summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the right upper quadrant, following a recent discharge for similar symptoms. With a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube placement due to prior anastomotic ulcer, she presented with burning pain, nausea, and decreased oral intake. A CT scan showed no acute intra-abdominal abnormality, abscess, or obstruction. Pain was managed with oxycodone and gabapentin, and hydration was optimized by increasing free water flushes to 100 mL every four hours. Her condition improved, and she was discharged home on oral pain medications with plans for follow-up in the pain clinic. She remained on her chronic medications for depression, anxiety, anemia, and hyperlipidemia, with no complications during the stay.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
